prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1094; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Claimant reports pain and swelling in the left wrist and has been advised to seek medical evaluation. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles uploaded to file.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant confirmed they are not represented by an attorney and wishes to handle the bodily injury portion directly. Explained the claims process, the documentation needed for medical expenses, and the timeline for review. Claimant reports diagnosis of a wrist fracture and a splint has been applied. Medical records authorization form sent for signature.

Entry 3: Signed medical authorization received. Requested records from the treating facility, including imaging results, the orthopedic consult, and treatment notes. Claimant states a follow-up appointment is scheduled for next week to evaluate whether surgical intervention will be needed. Noted that the claimant has missed some work and will provide wage documentation once available.

Entry 4: Vehicle damage appraisal completed on the insured's rear bumper and trunk area. Third-party vehicle inspected separately with damage to front bumper, hood, and radiator support. Liability appears clear based on the police report and statements from both drivers. Reserve adjusted to reflect the fracture diagnosis and anticipated treatment costs. Claimant advised again of the right to seek legal counsel at any time.

Entry 5: Received orthopedic follow-up notes confirming the fracture is healing and a cast has replaced the splint. Claimant reports ongoing limited grip strength and difficulty with daily tasks. Wage loss statement received from employer. File flagged for periodic review of medical status. Next contact with claimant scheduled to check on treatment progress and any further bills submitted.
